_instructions: Edit this list as the codebook changes. Each code needs a unique key (letters, numbers, underscores; it becomes the CSV column name), a short label shown on the toggle, and a definition shown under it. Do not rename a key after coding has started, or the old answers will export under the old column. Codes 1 to 9 get number-key shortcuts in the order listed.

codes.label: Tutorial / how-to
codes.definition: Post teaches or asks how to self-administer: mapping, placement, dosing, technique, beginner guides, cost of getting started.

codes.label: Seeks advice
codes.definition: Poster asks peers for guidance about a procedure or their appearance (help, advice, what should I do).

codes.label: Bodily or product risk
codes.definition: Discusses side effects, reactions, something going wrong, safety, or whether a product is safe to use.

codes.label: Product authenticity
codes.definition: Discusses whether a product is real or counterfeit, or how to verify it (QR codes, packaging, sellers, sourcing).

codes.label: Regulation / supply chain
codes.definition: Mentions FDA, customs, seizures, crackdowns, vendor changes, or other regulatory disruptions to getting products.

codes.label: Desire / transformation
codes.definition: Frames injectables as objects of desire, identity, or transformation (hauls, delivery day, finally did it, so happy).

codes.label: Justifies risk
codes.definition: Acknowledges risk and justifies doing it anyway (cost savings, distrust of providers or FDA, did my research).

codes.label: Research sources
codes.definition: Names or weighs information sources used in self-directed research (books, videos, clinicians, studies, other users).

codes.label: Clinician self-ID
codes.definition: Poster identifies as a medical professional (RN, NP, PA, MD, injector, esthetician).
